headline: A stormy week: back-to-back weather fronts bring rounds of rain, gusty winds, mountain snow and coastal flooding, with the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore under a minor coastal flood advisory today and heavier rain Wednesday night into Thursday that could push the Skokomish River to flood stage.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Showers are focused on the Olympic Peninsula this morning as low pressure lingers offshore, continuing into early afternoon, with a break for the Puget Sound lowlands later this morning while rain keeps going on the coast. Along the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore, including Sequim and Port Angeles, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 8 AM to 2 PM for minor flooding around this morning's high tide. Snow levels sit near 2,000–3,000 feet, and the Olympics pick up 4–8 inches under a Winter Weather Advisory until 4 PM, before snow levels rise to 3,000–4,500 feet this evening. The next front spreads widespread rain across the region late this evening, with rain returning to Seattle after about 4 PM.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Tuesday brings widespread rain and gusty southeast winds; in Seattle gusts near 23 mph are possible, mainly Tuesday morning, while a Wind Advisory covers the coast and western and southern Olympic foothills from 4 PM today to 4 PM Tuesday for gusts to 40 mph. Rain tapers Tuesday afternoon with highs in the low 50s, and snow levels rise to around 5,000 feet: Stevens Pass may get 1–3 inches and the North Cascades (such as Washington Pass) 4–8 inches, with a Winter Weather Advisory for the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades from 8 PM tonight to 10 PM Tuesday. Tides climb more noticeably along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday on, and forecasters are watching closely for possible flooding there. Another front arrives Wednesday with more widespread lowland rain, breezy winds and mountain snow.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The heaviest rain of the week is expected Wednesday night into Thursday, especially over the Olympics, where the Skokomish River is forecast to reach flood stage around midweek and possibly moderate flood stage; a Hydrologic Outlook is out, though no widespread river flooding is expected. High pressure is favored to rebuild late in the week, making Friday a break from the wind before it turns breezy again over the weekend.

coast: A Coastal Flood Warning covers the Grays Harbor County coast from 8 AM to 2 PM today for moderate to major flooding at this morning's high tide, especially in Westport and Ocean Shores, while a Coastal Flood Advisory covers the north coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca for minor flooding. Moderate to major coastal flooding is increasingly likely again on the Grays Harbor coast with Wednesday's tides, possibly made worse by high surf, and tides rise along the Strait and Puget Sound from Tuesday on. For boaters, a Storm Warning covers the outer coastal waters (10–60 miles out) from 7 AM today to 3 PM Tuesday for southeast gusts up to about 63 mph (55 knots); Gale Warnings cover the inner coastal waters and the east Strait entrance for gusts up to about 46 mph (40 knots); and Small Craft Advisories cover the central and west Strait, Admiralty Inlet, the northern inland waters and San Juan Islands, and the Grays Harbor bar, with winds about 23–35 mph (20–30 knots). Another front Wednesday into Thursday brings storm-force gusts possible on the coastal waters, gales on the east Strait and north waters, and a 30 percent chance of thunderstorms offshore. Seas of 10–12 feet today build to 18–22 feet Tuesday through Thursday, then ease to 10–12 feet Friday through the weekend; rough Grays Harbor bar conditions may become severe midweek.
watch_for: Tides rising along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday on, after today's minor coastal flood advisory for the Strait.
Heavy rain Wednesday night into Thursday, with the Skokomish River likely reaching flood stage and possibly moderate flood stage.
Moderate to major coastal flooding again on the Grays Harbor coast with Wednesday's high tides.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the active, wet and windy pattern through Thursday, with growing confidence in Wednesday's Grays Harbor coastal flooding, while the Strait and Puget Sound tide impacts and late-week details are still being monitored.
